text:
At the bottom of the parasol I see the marvelous prostitutes

with their slightly worn dress beside the forest-colored lamp.

They stroll with

a large piece of wallpaper,

like the old floors of a house being demolished

that one cannot contemplate without one’s heart tightening,

or a shell of white marble

torn from a mantelpiece,

or a net of those chains that behind them

become entangled.


The great instinct of combustion takes possession of the streets

where they remain

like roasted flowers.


Their eyes raise in the distance

a wind of stone in the mirrors,

while they plunge motionless

into the center of the whirlwind.


Nothing equals for me the meaning of their

careless thought,

the freshness of the stream in which their boots wet the shadow

of its peak,

the reality of those handfuls of cut hay in which

they disappear.


I see their breasts, which set a point of sunlight in the deep night,

where the time of bending and rising is the only

exact measure of life.


I see their breasts, stars upon waves,

their breasts

in which the invisible blue milk weeps forever.


Version by Manuel Álvarez Ortega

translation.title: An Absolutely White Man and Woman
translation.editorial_note: Translated from the supplied Spanish rendering of Breton, not recovered from the French original. The translator credit in the source is retained; the source’s deliberately unstable surreal syntax is left open.
